key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings with more disk-like splats and lower porosity deliver denser microstructures, better long-term corrosion resistance, and improved wear behavior in humid environments.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray parameters and ambient humidity can directly improve the durability of Fe-based protective coatings for steel components exposed to corrosion and sliding wear.
method: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings onto Q235 carbon steel
Compared coatings prepared under different spray parameters to link splat morphology, porosity, and microstructure
Evaluated long-term corrosion and tribological performance across different humidity conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports disk-like droplets with high circularity/expansion factor, reduced porosity in better coatings, and lower friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on controlling spray-induced porosity and environmental humidity, so results may not transfer directly to other substrates or service conditions without re-optimization.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
